questions.question: When was Hatsune Miku's original Japanese VOCALOID2 voicebank released?
Which date is specifically associated with Miku's original voicebank release anniversary?
questions.explanation: March 9 is Miku Day, but it is not the original voicebank's release date.

questions.question: Which pair consists entirely of Crypton Future Media's Piapro Characters?
questions.explanation: All four are real Vocaloid/virtual-singer characters, but only the selected pair are both Crypton Piapro Characters.

questions.question: Who produced the original “World is Mine”?
Which producer is associated with “Tell Your World”?
questions.explanation: All four options are major producers associated with Miku, making this a recognition question rather than an elimination question.

questions.question: Which song was created by wowaka?
Which description of Project SEKAI is most accurate?
options: A Miku-focused successor to Project DIVA
A voice-synthesis engine developed by Crypton
A rhythm/adventure game combining original characters with Virtual Singers
A concert platform for projecting Miku onto a screen
questions.explanation: Project SEKAI combines original human characters with Virtual Singer versions of Miku and the other Crypton characters.

questions.question: Which statement about Kasane Teto is correct?
options: She was originally created by Crypton as Miku's counterpart
She debuted as a Yamaha VOCALOID2 voicebank in 2008
She originated as an April Fools character and later became an UTAU voicebank
She was created specifically for Project SEKAI
questions.explanation: Teto originated in 2008 and subsequently became an actual singing-synthesis character through UTAU and later other synthesis platforms.

questions.question: Which song became a major Miku/Teto crossover phenomenon in the 2020s?
questions.explanation: “Mesmerizer” features both Hatsune Miku and Kasane Teto and was released by 32ki in 2024.

questions.question: Which song is most strongly associated with inabakumori?
questions.explanation: This is deliberately harder than asking for a famous Miku song: “Lagtrain” is strongly associated with inabakumori but features Kaai Yuki rather than Miku.

questions.question: Which song/producer pairing is correct?
options: The Disappearance of Hatsune Miku — cosMo@BousouP
questions.explanation: All four producers are genuine major Vocaloid names; only the pairing is correct.

questions.question: Which THREE statements about Kasane Teto are correct?
options: She is an official Crypton Piapro Character
She later received a Synthesizer V AI voice
She originated as an April Fools project
questions.explanation: Teto's official chronology records her April 2008 debut and subsequent UTAU development; she later expanded into newer synthesis platforms.

questions.question: Which THREE song/producer pairings are correct?
questions.explanation: This is intended to separate fans who recognise song titles from fans who actually know the producer catalogue.

questions.question: Which company created and released Hatsune Miku?
questions.explanation: Crypton Future Media (Sapporo) developed and released Miku as part of their Character Vocal Series. SEGA publishes the Project DIVA games; Yamaha created the VOCALOID engine itself.

questions.question: What is Hatsune Miku primarily?
options: A rhythm-game mascot created by SEGA
A human singer whose stage name is Miku
A virtual singer and singing voicebank character
A fictional idol who has never had a voicebank
questions.explanation: Miku is a voicebank for Yamaha's VOCALOID (and later NT) synthesis software, marketed as a virtual singer. She is not a human performer, nor is she limited to games.

questions.question: Who illustrated Miku's original character design?
questions.explanation: KEI designed the original box art and character illustration. iXima, Mogumo, and redjuice are well-known Vocaloid artists but did not create Miku's default design.

questions.question: Whose voice was used as the basis for Miku's original Japanese voicebank?
questions.explanation: Voice actress Saki Fujita provided the sampled phonemes. Crypton processed her recordings into the VOCALOID2 library.

questions.question: Which colour is most iconic in Miku's character design?
questions.explanation: Her signature colour is #39C5BB, a turquoise/cyan shade. This hex code even references '39.'

questions.question: What is the famous Japanese wordplay behind the number 39?
questions.explanation: San-kyuu (39) sounds like 'thank you' in Japanese. It is also read as mi-ku, which is why March 9 (3/9) is celebrated as 'Miku Day.'

questions.question: Which game series is most directly associated with Miku as its central rhythm-game character?
questions.explanation: The Project DIVA series (SEGA, 2009–present) is built around Miku as the central icon. Project SEKAI features her alongside original human characters, but DIVA is the classic Miku-centric rhythm franchise.

questions.question: In Vocaloid culture, what does 'producer' usually mean?
options: A person who manufactures the voicebank hardware
The manager of every official Miku concert
An illustrator who only draws character art
A creator who makes music using a voice-synthesis character
questions.explanation: A Vocaloid 'producer' is any musician/composer who writes, arranges, and tunes songs using Vocaloid/UTAU/SynthV voicebanks.

questions.question: What is a singing voicebank?
options: A collection of official concert recordings
A database containing every Vocaloid song
Recorded vocal material and data used by synthesis software
questions.explanation: A voicebank is a library of recorded phonemes (and, in modern engines, AI-trained vocal data) that the synthesis engine stitches into singing.

questions.question: Which song is associated with DECO*27?
questions.explanation: 'Ghost Rule' (2016) is one of DECO*27's biggest hits. 'Melt' is by ryo, 'Tell Your World' by kz, and 'Senbonzakura' by Kurousa-P.

questions.question: Which song is especially associated with producer Mitchie M?
questions.explanation: 'FREELY TOMORROW' (2011) is Mitchie M's breakthrough hit, famous for its ultra-realistic Miku tuning. It held the record for fastest Vocaloid song to reach the Niconico Hall of Legend.

questions.question: Which of these is a classic ryo/supercell Miku song?
questions.explanation: 'Melt' (2007) was ryo's debut Vocaloid work and helped launch the early Miku boom. 'Lagtrain' is by inabakumori, 'Bug' by Kairiki Bear, and 'Mesmerizer' by 32ki (Satsuki).

questions.question: Which three are strongly associated with the broader modern Miku / Vocaloid song landscape? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: 'Lagtrain' (2020), 'Mesmerizer' (2024), and 'Ghost Rule' (2016) span three different eras of Vocaloid. 'Bohemian Rhapsody' is by Queen and unrelated.

questions.question: In Project SEKAI, which group is particularly associated with the character Hatsune Miku in its Virtual Singer material?
options: All groups can feature Virtual Singer versions
questions.explanation: Every original unit in Project SEKAI has 'SEKAI' versions where Miku and other Virtual Singers appear with thematic outfits matching that unit's musical genre.

questions.question: Which visual feature is most strongly associated with Kasane Teto?
questions.explanation: Teto's signature look is red hair styled in twin drills (often mistaken for pigtails, which she supposedly hates). Turquoise twin tails belong to Miku.

questions.question: Who produced 'Mesmerizer'?
questions.explanation: 32ki, read as Satsuki (サツキ), is the producer. The music video was animated by channel, which sometimes causes confusion about authorship.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a Crypton Piapro Character?
questions.explanation: GUMI (Megpoid) is developed by Internet Co., Ltd. MEIKO, Kagamine Len, and KAITO are all part of Crypton's Character Vocal / Piapro series.

questions.question: Which pair consists of a Miku song and its correct producer?
questions.explanation: '39Music!' (2016) is by mikitoP. 'Tell Your World' is kz, 'Senbonzakura' is Kurousa-P, and 'Melt' is ryo.

questions.question: Which statement about Miku's live appearances is most accurate?
options: Every live Miku show uses a physical humanoid robot
Miku concerts are exclusively pre-recorded videos with no stage performance
She is commonly presented as a projected virtual performer with live musical accompaniment
Miku can only appear in Project DIVA concerts
questions.explanation: Miku concerts (Magical Mirai, Miku Expo, etc.) use Pepper's ghost / transparent screen projection with a live band. She is not a robot, and her appearances span many events beyond Project DIVA.

questions.question: Which three are Crypton Piapro Characters? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Crypton's Piapro Characters are Miku, Rin, Len, Luka, MEIKO, and KAITO. GUMI is from Internet Co., Ltd.

questions.question: Which three songs have been featured in Project SEKAI's Virtual Singer / song ecosystem? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: 'Melt,' 'World is Mine,' and '39Music!' are all pre-existing songs in Project SEKAI's Virtual Singer category. 'Bad Apple!!' is a Touhou Project song; while a SEKAI-arranged version exists, it is not part of the core Virtual Singer classic catalogue in the same context.

questions.question: Which three producers are strongly associated with Miku songs? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: DECO*27, kz, and ryo are legendary Miku producers. Hikakin is a Japanese YouTuber/beatboxer, not a Vocaloid producer.

questions.question: Which three clues point toward Miku's '39' association? (Select all that apply)
options: '39' is used prominently in Miku-related song titles
March 9 is celebrated by fans as Miku Day
Miku's original voicebank was released in 1939
questions.explanation: Songs like '39' (sasakure.UK) and '39Music!' reference the number; san-kyuu = 'thank you'; and March 9 is Miku Day. Miku was released in 2007, not 1939.

questions.question: A player says: 'Teto is just another Crypton VOCALOID, like Miku.' What is the best correction?
options: Teto and Miku were released together by Crypton in 2007
Teto is simply Miku's alternate costume
Teto has a different origin and voice-synthesis history; she began with UTAU and later expanded to other synthesis platforms
Teto is a Project SEKAI-original character created for the game
questions.explanation: Teto was created by 2channel users as an April Fools' prank, released on UTAU, and later got Synthesizer V and VOICEPEAK versions via AH-Software/TWINDRILL. She is not Crypton-made, nor is she a Project SEKAI original.

questions.question: Which chronology is the most accurate?
options: Project SEKAI launches → Miku debuts → Project DIVA launches → Teto is created
Miku debuts in 2007 → Project DIVA era → Project SEKAI era → Teto's major modern crossover visibility
Miku debuts → Teto is created → Project DIVA launches → Project SEKAI launches
Teto is created → Miku debuts → Project SEKAI launches → Project DIVA launches
questions.explanation: Miku debuted 2007 → Project DIVA began 2009 → Teto was created 2008 as a prank/UTAU but her major modern crossover visibility exploded with Synthesizer V (2023) and 'Mesmerizer' (2024) → Project SEKAI launched 2020. Option B is the only sequence that correctly orders the eras of mainstream visibility.

questions.question: Which statement best captures why Miku remains culturally distinctive?
options: She is a shared creative platform: different producers, games, fans, and performers can reinterpret the same virtual singer
She is a fixed fictional character whose songs, design, and personality are controlled entirely by one studio
Her popularity comes mainly from one game rather than music creators
Her catalogue is limited to officially released songs written by Crypton
questions.explanation: Miku's enduring power comes from her status as an open creative platform. Thousands of independent producers, illustrators, dancers, and game developers have built a decentralized culture around her — something no single studio could control.
